arte.universo: Germany and Greenland in the 1910s to 1930s: an early 20th-century university lecture hall with wooden benches and a big hand-drawn world map, a scientist's study with paper maps and an oil lamp, a dry fossil dig, the endless white ice sheet of Greenland; then a 1960s research ship on the night ocean, and modern Mexico City at dusk with volcanoes on the horizon. No portraits and no recognizable real people: the scientist is never shown, only his maps and objects. Anonymous people only from behind or far away.

escena.accion: In a dim early 20th-century university lecture hall, a large hand-drawn map on the front wall shows Africa and South America pushed together like puzzle pieces; anonymous men in old suits on wooden benches are seen from behind, some leaning back as if laughing
escena.protagonista: The Pasita, lower-middle, seen from behind, small school backpack, standing in the aisle looking up at the map
escena.objeto: The big wall map with two continents fitted together, no text
escena.foreground: The back of a wooden bench and a bowler hat, slightly blurred
escena.midground: The Pasita in the aisle, anonymous audience silhouettes
escena.background: The map lit by a single lamp, tall dark windows
escena.iluminacion: Warm lamp light on the map, cold shadows over the audience
escena.emocion: Disbelief in the room, the Pasita alone believing
escena.composicion: Wide shot from the back of the hall; the upper 42% is the dark ceiling and wall above the map

escena.accion: On a wooden desk lit by an oil lamp, the Pasita slides two paper cut-out continents, Africa and South America, until their coasts fit together perfectly
escena.protagonista: The Pasita, lower-right, leaning over the desk with both hands on the paper pieces, eyes wide
escena.objeto: Two paper cut-out continents fitting together like puzzle pieces on top of an old world map, no text
escena.foreground: A pencil, scissors and an ink pot, slightly blurred
escena.midground: The Pasita and the fitted paper continents
escena.background: Dark study with rolled maps and a globe on a shelf
escena.iluminacion: Warm oil-lamp light from one side, deep shadows
escena.composicion: Medium shot from slightly above; the upper 42% dark background

cuerpo: Del mismo reptil, en Brasil y **Sudáfrica**.

escena.accion: In a dry rocky landscape at dusk, the Pasita kneels and brushes dust off the fossil skeleton of a small slender reptile embedded in a flat grey rock
escena.protagonista: The Pasita, lower-left, kneeling, holding a small brush, focused
escena.objeto: A small lizard-like reptile fossil skeleton in pale grey stone
escena.foreground: Rock fragments and a small hammer, slightly blurred
escena.background: Flat dry plain and distant hills under a dark dusk sky
escena.iluminacion: Low warm last sunlight on the fossil, cool shadows
escena.composicion: Medium shot; the upper 42% dark dusk sky

cuerpo: No sabía explicar **qué fuerza los movía**.

escena.accion: On the endless white ice sheet of Greenland at twilight, the Pasita stands quietly beside a pair of old wooden skis planted upright in the snow, looking toward the empty horizon
escena.protagonista: The Pasita, lower-middle, seen from behind, backpack on, small in the vast landscape, still and respectful
escena.objeto: A pair of old wooden skis standing upright in the snow
escena.background: Flat endless ice, a faint distant line of a sled trail
escena.iluminacion: Cold blue twilight, a thin pale glow on the horizon
escena.emocion: Quiet sadness and respect, nothing dramatic
escena.composicion: Wide shot; the upper 42% is the dark twilight sky

cuerpo: El Atlántico se abre **2.5 cm al año**.

escena.accion: At night on the deck of a 1960s research ship on a calm dark ocean, the Pasita leans over the railing and looks down; deep below, a long glowing crack in the sea floor shines faintly lime green
escena.protagonista: The Pasita, lower-right, leaning on the railing, seen from behind, backpack on
escena.objeto: A long glowing crack in the ocean floor visible through the dark water
escena.foreground: Ship railing, coiled ropes and an old measuring instrument, slightly blurred
escena.background: Dark calm ocean meeting a starry night sky
escena.iluminacion: Cold moonlight, a soft lime glow from the depths
escena.composicion: Medium-wide shot; the upper 42% is the dark starry sky

cuerpo: La placa de Cocos se mete **bajo la nuestra**.

escena.accion: At dusk on a calm Mexico City rooftop with water tanks and clotheslines, the Pasita looks at a smoking volcano and a snowy volcano far away on the horizon above the city lights
escena.protagonista: The Pasita, lower-left, seen from behind, school backpack on, sitting on the rooftop edge
escena.objeto: Two distant volcanoes, one with a thin plume of smoke
escena.foreground: A rooftop water tank and clothesline, slightly blurred
escena.background: The city lights spreading to the volcanoes on the horizon
escena.iluminacion: Deep blue dusk, warm city lights below
escena.emocion: Calm understanding, the ground is alive
escena.composicion: Wide shot; the upper 42% is the dark dusk sky

post:
En 1912, Alfred Wegener dijo que los continentes se mueven. Casi nadie le creyó. 🌎

Se dio cuenta de que África y Sudamérica encajan como piezas de rompecabezas, y de que había fósiles del mismo reptil en Brasil y en Sudáfrica. Pero no sabía explicar qué fuerza los movía, y muchos geólogos lo tacharon de disparate. Murió en 1930 en una expedición en Groenlandia.

En los años 60, el fondo del mar le dio la razón: el Atlántico se abre unos 2.5 cm al año. Y por eso tiembla en México: la placa de Cocos se mete bajo la Norteamericana.

¿Alguna vez tuviste razón y nadie te creyó? 👇
